How fast an eigenvector decays

Source: R/jacobi.R
decay_rate.Rd

Outside the window the eigenvalue equation is the free recurrence `b (u[j-1] + u[j+1]) + a u[j] = lambda u[j]`, whose solutions are `z^j` for the two roots of `z^2 - mu z + 1` with `mu = (lambda - a_inf) / b_inf`. The roots are reciprocal, so for `|mu| > 2` exactly one lies inside the unit disc, and membership in `l^2` forces it on each side. An eigenvector is therefore *exactly* geometric outside the window, at the rate this returns, rather than asymptotically so.

Usage

decay_rate(A, lambda)

Arguments

A

A `linop` from [linop_jacobi()], or a [finite_section()] of one.

lambda

One or more real values.

Value

A numeric vector in `(0, 1)`, with `NA` where `lambda` lies in the essential spectrum.

Details

`NA` for a value inside the essential spectrum: there both roots lie on the unit circle, nothing decays, and there is no eigenvector to decay.

Examples

H <- linop_jacobi(diagonal = 1)
## the golden-ratio conjugate, for the eigenvalue sqrt(5)
decay_rate(H, sqrt(5))
decay_rate(H, 0)
